name: Inkvolt Print
subtitle: Printer status, ink and toner
promotionalText: See every printer's status, ink and toner levels and alerts at a glance, in its window or from the menu bar. No account, no cloud, no tracking.
description: Inkvolt Print keeps an eye on your printers. It finds them on your network and shows what matters: ready or asleep, ink and toner levels, paper and cover problems, and how many pages they've printed, kept up to date while it runs.
• Finds the printers on your network by itself.
• Ink and toner levels with the pages left, and the cartridge to buy when one runs low.
• Paper jams, empty trays, open covers and other problems, in plain words.
• A menu bar item shows at a glance whether every printer is fine, and a notification tells you when one needs you.
• Made for HP printers and works with Canon, Epson, Brother and other AirPrint, Mopria or IPP Everywhere printers. Older network printers get status and toner over SNMP.
• Before it shows anything, it checks that the device at a printer's address is still your printer, so another device that took the address is never shown under its name.
• Printers set up in macOS show too, USB and shared ones included, with their status and your print jobs, which you can cancel.
• A printer that stopped printing gets step-by-step help: Inkvolt Print finds it at a new address, resumes a paused queue and cancels stuck jobs, and says what to do in System Settings for the rest.

• Scan from the printer's scanner or a USB scanner: blank pages left out, crooked pages straightened, pages turned, cropped and reordered before you save them as a PDF, a searchable PDF (text recognised on your Mac) or JPEG images. One-click scan presets save where you choose, and can print a copy or attach the files to an email.

• Scan a stack from the feeder and split it into separate files at separator sheets or blank pages. Lay several photos on the glass and each is saved on its own, cut out straight; adjust any of them by hand.
• Print a PDF, make a copy, or copy both sides of an ID card onto one page.
• Print photos at their real size (full page, standard photo sizes, contact sheets) on the printer's own paper sizes, borderless where it offers it, with the paper type and quality you pick.
• Set up a network printer in macOS with one click, so every app can print to it.
• Change an HP printer's settings (sleep, two-sided printing, paper) and its automatic firmware updates, and run its maintenance pages.
• Add a printer that doesn't announce itself: Inkvolt Print searches your network for it, or takes its address.
• A demo with made-up printers, to try it without one.
Private by design: no account, no cloud service, no ads, no analytics, no tracking. Inkvolt Print talks only to the printers on your network.
Free and open source (MIT License). Source code: https://github.com/gabandres/inkvolt

Inkvolt Print is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by HP Inc., Canon, Seiko Epson or Brother. HP is a trademark of HP Inc. Canon, Epson and Brother are trademarks of their owners. They are used only to describe the printers Inkvolt Print works with.
reviewNotes: Inkvolt Print reads the status, alerts and ink or toner levels of printers on the user's local network. There is no account or sign-in.

Without a printer: when none is found (after about 30 seconds of looking), the window says "No printers found" and offers "Try the Demo", which opens a second window with made-up printers (five on the network, three set up in macOS) that answer from data built into the app (nothing goes to the network).

In the demo window: the Scan tab (on the demo inkjet or the USB laser) scans made-up pages and saves them where you choose; the demo office laser's Fix It… shows the offline fixer; the office MFP's print queue card shows made-up jobs; Print a PDF and Print Photos open the macOS print panel (Cancel stops them); the demo printer's Settings tab takes changes but the made-up printer keeps none.

Local Network: macOS asks for Local Network access at first launch. The app uses it to find printers with Bonjour (the service types listed in NSBonjourServices) and to read them over HTTP and HTTPS (IPP, and HP's own LEDM and CDM interfaces) and over SNMP. If access is denied, the app says so and links to System Settings.

Entitlements: com.apple.security.network.client for those connections; com.apple.security.network.server for two things: (1) to receive the UDP replies to the SNMP requests the app sends to printers on port 161 (how it reads a printer's status and supply levels, and how the network search finds printers: one request to the subnet's broadcast address); in the App Sandbox, receiving those replies needs this entitlement: we tested a sandboxed build without it, and the request went out but receiving the printer's reply failed with EPERM; (2) new in 1.4.0, scanning with a phone: Scan tab › Use Your Phone… opens a window with a QR code, and only while that window is open the app serves one HTTPS page on TCP port 9781 of the local network, where the user's phone takes photos of pages and sends them to the app (only the first phone to open the page can send; closing the window stops the server). Nothing listens at any other time; com.apple.security.print to read the printers set up in macOS (their CUPS queues: USB printers and printers shared from other computers are listed with their status) and to cancel the user's own print jobs, through libcups; com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-write to save scans where the user chooses in the save panel; com.apple.security.files.bookmarks.app-scope to remember the folder the user chose for a scan preset; com.apple.security.device.usb to scan with USB scanners through ImageCaptureCore; com.apple.security.application-groups (AE6TTXW92K.com.bermudezsystems.inkvolt, our team's group) to keep an optional Inkvolt Pro licence key in one file that our other app, Inkvolt PDF, reads too, so a key entered in either app counts in both, and a list of the printers it knows (their names and network addresses, no keys or settings) that Inkvolt PDF reads to show a printer's status in its print panel. No key is needed: everything in the app works without one, and the app sells nothing. New in 1.4.0: com.apple.security.device.camera to scan with a camera (Scan tab › Use a Camera…, a webcam, document camera or iPhone through Continuity Camera): macOS asks for camera access only when that window opens; frames are kept only as the pages the user captures, nothing is recorded or sent; com.apple.security.personal-information.location for File › Set Up a New Printer's Wi-Fi…: macOS gives Wi-Fi network names only to apps with location access, so the app asks for it only from that guide (never at launch or anywhere else), to find a new printer's setup network nearby; the location itself is never read, used or kept, and the app never joins a network or sees a Wi-Fi password. Both usage descriptions say so (English and Spanish).
The app collects no data. Everything it remembers stays in its container on the Mac.
whatsNew: New in Inkvolt Print 1.4.0:

• Scan with a camera: Use a Camera… takes pages from your webcam, document camera or iPhone. Use Your Phone… takes photos of pages from any phone's browser, over your own Wi-Fi, while its window is open.
• Smarter scans: both sides on a one-sided feeder, pages turned upright on their own, a pen's color or punch holes cleaned away, two halves of a large original joined, and batches split at QR codes.
• Scan presets save Word or text files, smaller black-and-white PDFs, PDF/A or password-protected PDFs, and can name the file from the page's text.
• Recent Scans…: the last 20 scans, to open, email or print again.
• More ways to print: the clipboard (⇧⌘V), both sides by hand on a one-sided printer, several pages per sheet, booklets and posters, and cards, calendars and collages in Print Photos.
• Window › Print Log: every job this Mac printed, with each month's pages per printer and per person.
• Set up a new printer's Wi-Fi, see whether a printer needs its maker's driver, and share a printer with iPhones and iPads.
• Pages left on more printers, the printer's own panel message, more SNMPv3 options, and printers added or removed in macOS shown within seconds.
Novedades de Inkvolt Print 1.4.0:

• Escanear con una cámara: Usar una cámara… toma páginas de tu cámara web, tu cámara de documentos o tu iPhone. Usar tu teléfono… toma fotos de páginas desde el navegador de cualquier teléfono, por tu propia red Wi-Fi, mientras su ventana está abierta.

• Escaneos más inteligentes: ambas caras en un alimentador de una cara, páginas puestas al derecho solas, el color de un bolígrafo o las perforaciones limpiados, dos mitades de un original grande unidas y lotes divididos en códigos QR.
• Los ajustes de escaneo guardan archivos de Word o de texto, PDF más pequeños en blanco y negro, PDF/A o PDF con contraseña, y pueden nombrar el archivo con el texto de la página.
• Escaneos recientes…: los últimos 20 escaneos, para abrirlos, enviarlos por correo o imprimirlos de nuevo.
• Más formas de imprimir: el portapapeles (⇧⌘V), a doble cara a mano en una impresora de una cara, varias páginas por hoja, folletos y pósteres, y tarjetas, calendarios y collages en Imprimir fotos.
• Ventana › Registro de impresión: cada trabajo que imprimió este Mac, con las páginas de cada mes por impresora y por persona.
• Configura la Wi-Fi de una impresora nueva, mira si una impresora necesita el controlador de su fabricante y comparte una impresora con iPhone y iPad.
• Páginas restantes en más impresoras, el mensaje del panel de la impresora, más opciones de SNMPv3, y las impresoras agregadas o quitadas en macOS aparecen en segundos.
Novidades do Inkvolt Print 1.4.0:

• Digitalize com uma câmera: Usar uma câmera… captura páginas da sua webcam, câmera de documentos ou iPhone. Usar seu telefone… tira fotos de páginas pelo navegador de qualquer telefone, pela sua própria rede Wi-Fi, enquanto a janela estiver aberta.

• Digitalizações mais inteligentes: frente e verso em um alimentador de um lado, páginas colocadas na vertical sozinhas, remoção de cor de caneta ou furos de perfurador, união de duas metades de um original grande e divisão de lotes em códigos QR.
• Predefinições de digitalização salvam arquivos Word ou texto, PDFs menores em preto e branco, PDF/A ou PDFs protegidos por senha, e podem nomear o arquivo a partir do texto da página.
• Digitalizações recentes…: as últimas 20 digitalizações, para abrir, enviar por e-mail ou imprimir novamente.

• Mais formas de imprimir: área de transferência (⇧⌘V), frente e verso manualmente em uma impressora de um lado, várias páginas por folha, livretos e pôsteres, além de cartões, calendários e colagens em Imprimir fotos.
• Janela › Registro de impressão: todos os trabalhos que este Mac imprimiu, com as páginas de cada mês por impressora e por pessoa.
• Configure o Wi-Fi de uma impressora nova, veja se uma impressora precisa do driver do fabricante e compartilhe uma impressora com iPhones e iPads.
• Páginas restantes em mais impressoras, a mensagem do painel da impressora, mais opções de SNMPv3, e impressoras adicionadas ou removidas no macOS exibidas em segundos.
